# Memory search (memory.search)

## categories

[
  "memory"
]

## demonstrations

[
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "entries": []
    },
    "id": "basic",
    "input": {
      "query": "idea"
    },
    "title": "Empty workspace memory example"
  }
]

## description

Find memory entries by literal substring in their keys or values. Memory is agent-owned state at .memory.sqlite in the workspace. NOTES.md is the convention for free-form working notes; it is not created automatically. Memory contains no permissions or supervisor state. Read operations return an empty list before the first write.

## failure_modes

[
  {
    "condition": "Database is corrupt, locked or inaccessible.",
    "recovery": "Use working notes in NOTES.md; memory may need restoring from a checkpoint.",
    "symptom": "Capability error."
  }
]

## limitations

[
  "Values are text, at most 20000 characters; keys are at most 128 characters.",
  "Listing/search return at most 100 entries, ordered by key; no embeddings.",
  "Search case folding uses SQLite lower (ASCII); the substring is literal, not a SQL pattern.",
  "The agent may overwrite its own database with workspace tools; corruption is an error."
]
